name: 孟加拉豆娘魚
intro: Abudefduf bengalensis, known as the Bengal sergeant or the narrow-banded sergeant major, is a species of damselfish in the family Pomacentridae. It is a marine species native to the tropical Indo-Pacific, where it ranges from the eastern Indian Ocean to Australia and Japan in the Pacific Ocean.

name: 雜色豆娘魚
intro: The dusky sergeant (Abudefduf concolor), also known as the night sergeant, is a species of damselfish in the family Pomacentridae endemic to the eastern Pacific Ocean. The species can reach 19 cm (7.5 in) in total length.
distribution: Abudefduf concolor is found in the Eastern Pacific, from El Salvador to Peru, including the Galapagos, Cocos and Malpelo Islands.
behavior: Abudefduf concolor is a marine species found in shallow reef habitats, primarily rocky inshore reefs, at depths of up to 5 m (16 ft). It is an omnivorous fish that is also oviparous, with individuals forming pairs during breeding and males guarding and aerating eggs.

photo.author: loarie
photo.caption: Abudefduf concolor, Puntarenas Province, Costa Rica

name: 巴西刺鮨
intro: The Argentine seabass (Acanthistius brasilianus) is a species of seabass in the family Serranidae. It occurs on the South American continental shelf of the western Atlantic Ocean, where it used to be caught commercially for human consumption.
distribution: The Argentine seabass is a rare species, found only in the southwestern Atlantic Ocean, along the coasts of Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil. They generally inhabit cold waters along the South American continental shelf, but also form a component of some subtropical reef communities, especially rocky reefs and outcrops.

photo.author: Carlos A. Rangel
photo.caption: Acanthistius brasilianus at Ilha Redonda, Monumento Natural das Ilhas Cagarras, Brazil.

name: 環帶刺鮨

It is native to the southern Pacific Ocean, where it occurs along the coasts of eastern Australia and New Zealand.

photo.author: Susan Prior

name: 睛斑刺鮨

intro: Acanthogobius flavimanus, commonly referred to as the yellowfin goby, mahaze, and Japanese river goby, is a goby native to the northwestern Pacific Ocean. It has spread beyond its native range to become an introduced, and often invasive, species.
distribution: Acanthogobius flavimanus is native to northeastern Asia. The fish's native range includes the Bohai Sea, the Yellow Sea, Primorsky Krai, and the Japanese archipelago. Generally, the yellowfin goby is a bottom dwelling fish, which inhabits bays and estuaries.

name: 心斑刺尾魚
intro: Acanthurus achilles, the Achilles tang, redtail surgeonfish or redspot surgeonfish, is a marine ray-finned fish in the family Acanthuridae, the surgeonfishes, unicornfishes and tangs. This fish is found in various part of the Pacific Ocean.
distribution: Acanthurus achilles is found in various reefs of Oceania, up to the islands of Hawaii and Pitcairn. It is also, although less commonly, found in the Mariana Islands and even some reefs in southern Mexico and Guatemala. It is a benthopelagic species which inhabits the clear waters on the seaward side of reefs.
behavior: Acanthurus achilles is herbivorous, grazing largely on benthic algae. It is territorial and monogamous.

photo.caption: Achilles Tang (Acanthurus achilles)

intro: Acanthurus albipectoralis, the whitefin surgeonfish, is a species of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the family Acanthuridae, the surgeonfishes, unicornfishes and tangs. This species is found in the Western Pacific Ocean.
distribution: Acanthurus albipectoralis is found in the southwestern Pacific Ocean from eastern Australia to Tonga. They are found on the exposed outer slopes of reefs, typically in small groups high in the water column feeding on zooplankton.

distribution: Acanthurus auranticavus is found in the Indian and Western PacificOceans. In the Indian Ocean it has been reported from the Maldives and the Seychelles, and recently Christmas Island.

distribution: Acanthurus leucosternon is found in tropical waters from the Indian Ocean. The species inhabits shallow and clear coastal waters always associated with a reef. It prefers flat top reefs and areas along seaward slopes.
behavior: The powder blue tang, like most fish in the family Acanthuridae, is herbivorous, eating mostly benthic algae. Acanthurus leucosternon has a diurnal activity. It is solitary, territorial and aggressive with other surgeonfish.

name: 綠藍唇魚
intro: The eastern blue groper (Achoerodus viridis) is a species of wrasse native to southeastern Australia from Hervey Bay in southern Queensland to Wilsons Promontory in Victoria. They occur in coastal waters, preferring rocky areas at a depth of about 40 m (130 ft). Juveniles inhabit beds of seagrass in estuaries.
distribution: The eastern blue groper is native to the southeastern coast of Australia. Its range extends from Mooloolaba in southern Queensland southwards to Wilsons Promontory in the south of Victoria, including the eastern end of the Bass Strait. Its habitat is rocky areas down to a depth of about 40 m (131 ft).
behavior: The eastern blue groper feeds mainly on crabs, shrimps, molluscs and echinoderms. Juvenile fish live in seagrass beds, where their diet is primarily small crustaceans. This fish is a monandric sequential hermaphrodite, always starting life as a female and becoming a male when it has reached a length of at least 60 cm (24 in).

name: 長鰭鱥
intro: The longfin dace (Agosia chrysogaster) is a species of freshwater fish in the leuciscid family of order Cypriniformes. It is the only member of the monotypic genus Agosia and is found in southwestern North America. The Gila longfin dace is considered the nominate subspecies, and the Yaqui longfin dace is considered a form.
distribution: Longfin dace are native to the deserts of southwestern North America, notably in the American states of Arizona and New Mexico and northern Mexico states of Sinaloa and Sonora. The longfin dace is tolerant to a wide range of water temperature, and is found in low elevation desert streams to mountain brooks.
behavior: Longfin dace are omnivorous and opportunistic feeders. They can feed on invertebrates, zooplankton, algae, and detritus.

photo.author: Alina Martin
photo.caption: Longfin Dace (Agosia chrysogaster) in the United States

distribution: The knife livebearer is native to the Central American countries of Costa Rica, Panama and Nicaragua.
behavior: Alfaro cultratus is insectivorous, taking aquatic insects as juveniles and moving onto terrestrial insects in adulthood. Like most American poeciliids, the knife livebearers reproduce ovoviviparously. After a gestation period of 24 days, the female gives birth to 10 to 30 young, seldom more.

name: 無斑鴛鴛鮨
intro: Alphestes immaculatus, the Pacific mutton hamlet, is a species of marine ray-finned fish which is classified within the subfamily Epinephelinae, the groupers, in the family Serranidae which also includes the anthias and sea basses. It is a predatory fish of the rocky coastlines of the eastern Pacific Ocean.
distribution: Alphestes immaculatusis found in the Eastern Pacific Ocean from southern Baja California and the Gulf of California south as far as Peru. It is also found around the Islas Marías and Revillagigedos of Mexico, the Galápagos, Malpelo Island in Colombia and Cocos Island in Costa Rica.
behavior: Alphestes immaculatus  is a secretive, camouflaged species of shallow water found in sea grass beds and rocky reefs at depths between 1 and 50 metres (3 ft 3 in and 164 ft 1 in). During the day it stays hidden in crevices or lying among seaweed, relying on their cryptic colouration to escape detection by predators.

distribution: The Pacific leaping blenny is a tropical blenny found in reefs in Samoa and the Marianas, Society, and Cook Islands, in the western and southern Pacific Ocean. The blennies are noted for leaping from hole to hole in the limestone rocks they inhabit, when disturbed; each of the common names for the species is derived from this.

distribution: Convict cichlids are native to the lakes and streams of Central America. In particular, the species occurs along the eastern coast of Central America from Guatemala to Costa Rica, and on the western coast from Honduras to Panama.
behavior: In natural habitats, the species has an omnivorous diet composed of plants, algae and various prey including small fish, crustaceans, insects and worms. 2% of its standard length, allowing it to have a varied diet. In the Indian Ocean, they are found in the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden, eastern Africa, Madagascar, Seychelles, the Persian Gulf, the Arabian Sea, the Maldives, Sri Lanka, the Andaman Sea, Australia, and Indonesia.

intro: Nemateleotris decora, the elegant firefish or purple firefish, is a species of dartfish native to tropical waters in the Indo-West Pacific, from Mauritius to Samoa, north to Ryukyu Islands, and south to New Caledonia, from depths ranging between 25 and 70 m (82 and 230 ft).

photo.author: TANAKA Juuyoh
photo.caption: Nemateleotris decora -42m in Mactan Cebu, Philippines

name: 雷达鱼
intro: Nemateleotris magnifica, known by a variety of common names including fire goby, magnificent fire fish, fire dartfish, or red fire goby, is a species of dartfish native to coral reefs of the Indian and Pacific oceans.

photo.author: Rickard Zerpe
photo.caption: Fire dartfish (Nemateleotris magnifica). Exploration diving around the island of Rao west of Morotai in Indonesia, June 2018.

name: 火焰鹰鱼
intro: The flame hawkfish (Neocirrhites armatus) is a species of marine ray-finned fish, a hawkfish belonging to the family Cirrhitidae. It is native to tropical reefs of the Pacific Ocean at depths of from 1 to 10 metres (3.3 to 32.8 ft). This species is also found in the aquarium trade.  It is the only known member of its genus.

photo.author: Brian Gratwicke
photo.caption: Flame Hawkfish

name: Elephant Ear Gourami
intro: The elephant ear gourami (Osphronemus exodon) is a large species of gourami native to the Mekong river basin in Thailand, Laos, and Cambodia and Vietnam.

photo.author: Ngo Van Tri
photo.caption: Osphronemus exodon, Dak Dam Stream, Sre Pok River, Dak Lak province, 2004, 19cm

name: Giant Red Tail Gourami
intro: The giant red tail gourami (Osphronemus laticlavius) is a large species of gourami belonging to the family Osphronemidae. This endangered fish is native to the Southeast Asian island of Borneo, where only known from the Kinabatangan and Segama river basins in Sabah, East Malaysia.

photo.author: Hectonichus
photo.caption: Adult Osphronemus laticlavius, on display at the Museo di Storia Naturale e del Territorio, Calci (Province Pisa), Italy

name: 玫瑰鲃
intro: The rosy barb (Pethia conchonius) is a subtropical freshwater cyprinid fish found in southern Asia from Afghanistan to Bangladesh.

photo.author: The Great Mule of Eupatoria
photo.caption: A school of Rosy barbs at an aquarium in a public aquarium store

name: 奥德萨鲃
intro: The Odessa barb (Pethia padamya) is a species of cyprinid fish known from Central Myanmar, where it is known to occur in an artificial pond above the Anisakan Falls and also from the lower Chindwin River.

photo.author: Waitingonthetide
photo.caption: Photo of Puntius Padamya or Odessa barb

name: 刚果灯
intro: The Congo tetra (Phenacogrammus interruptus) is a species of fish in the African tetra family, found in the central Congo River Basin in Africa. It is commonly kept in aquaria.

photo.author: André Karwath aka Aka
photo.caption: This image shows a Congo Tetra (Phenacogrammus interruptus).

name: 帆鳍玛丽
intro: The sailfin molly (Poecilia latipinna) is a livebearer fish typically found in both freshwater and brackish waterways along the East Coast of the United States, from North Carolina south to Florida, and around the Gulf of Mexico to Texas, and south to the Yucatán Peninsula of Mexico.

photo.author: (c) Nick Tobler (Cowturtle), some rights reserved (CC BY)
photo.caption: Photo of Sailfin Molly (undefined) uploaded from iNaturalist.

name: 孔雀鱼
intro: The guppy (Poecilia reticulata), also known as the peacock fish, millionfish or rainbow fish, is a member of the family Poeciliidae and, akin to most New World members of the family, is classified as a livebearer. Male guppies, which are smaller than females, have ornamental caudal and dorsal fins.

photo.author: Per Harald Olsen
photo.caption: Wild guppies (Poecilia reticulata). Male above, and 2 females below.

name: 玛丽鱼
intro: Poecilia sphenops, called the Mexican molly or simply the molly, is a species of poeciliid fish from Central America. It was once understood as a widespread species with numerous local variants ranging from Mexico to Venezuela, but these variants are today considered distinct species belonging to the P. sphenops complex and P.

photo.author: (c) James-LaFontaine, some rights reserved (CC BY)
photo.caption: Photo of Common Molly (undefined) uploaded from iNaturalist.

name: 安德勒孔雀鱼
intro: Poecilia wingei, known to aquarists as Endlers or Endler's livebearer, in the genus Poecilia, is a small fish native to the Paria Peninsula in Venezuela. They are prolific breeders and often hybridize with guppies.

photo.author: Emilio17
photo.caption: Poecilia wingei, Campoma-Guppy, male, population from locus typicus. The fish is a descendant from the population which is called "P. wingei Ca" in Table1. name: 比夫拉多板盾尾魚
intro: Prionurus biafraensis, the Biafra doctorfish, is a species of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the family Acanthuridae, the surgeonfishes, unicornfishes and tangs. This fish is found in the eastern Atlantic Ocean.

photo.author: thibaudaronson
photo.caption: Prionurus biafraensis, Bom Bom, Principe, São Tomé & Príncipe

name: 六线龙
intro: The six-line wrasse (Pseudocheilinus hexataenia) is a species of marine ray-finned fish from the family Labridae which has a wide Indo-Pacific distribution. This species is associated with coral reefs and can be found in the aquarium trade.

photo.author: Brian Gratwicke
photo.caption: Six Line Wrasse - Pseudocheilinus hexataenia

name: 兰花拟雀鲷
intro: Pseudochromis fridmani is a species of fish in the family Pseudochromidae, the dottybacks. Its common name is orchid dottyback. It is endemic to the Red Sea. 3 centimeters long. It lives in tropical marine waters up to 60 meters deep near reefs. It shelters in holes and under overhangs.

photo.author: Diego Delso
photo.caption: Orchid dottyback (Pseudochromis fridmani), Jeddah, Saudi Arabia

name: 叉尾蓝眼
intro: The forktail blue-eye (Pseudomugil furcatus) is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish in the family Pseudomugilidae. It is endemic to Papua New Guinea, south-east of Popondetta, where it is found in rainforest streams.

photo.author: R.workoran
photo.caption: Forktail Blue-eye

name: 米字蓝眼
intro: The spotted blue-eye (Pseudomugil gertrudae), also known as the delicate blue-eye, Gertrude's blue-eye, or northern blue-eye, is a species of freshwater ray-finned fish in the family Pseudomugilidae. It is native to Indonesia, Papua New Guinea and northern Australia.

photo.author: Der Regenbogenfisch (Diskussion)
photo.caption: Spotted Blue Eye (Pseudomugil gertrudae)

name: 虎皮鱼
intro: The tiger barb or Sumatra barb (Puntigrus tetrazona), is a species of tropical cyprinid fish.

photo.author: Malene Thyssen
photo.caption: Tiger barb (Puntius tetrazona; accepted as Puntigrus tetrazona)

name: 樱桃鲃
intro: The cherry barb (Rohanella titteya) is a tropical freshwater fish belonging to the family Cyprinidae.  It is endemic to Sri Lanka, and introduced populations have become established in Mexico and Colombia. The cherry barb was named Puntius titteya by Paules Edward Pieris Deraniyagala in 1929.

photo.author: Brian Gratwicke
photo.caption: Cherry barb (Puntius titteya)

name: 剪刀波鱼
intro: Rasbora trilineata is a species of ray-finned fish in the genus Rasbora. Common names include scissortail rasbora and three-lined rasbora. It comes from Southeast Asia. Its length is up to 15 cm (6").

photo.author: Lerdsuwa
photo.caption: Three-lined rasbora Rasbora trilineata

name: 食藻鳚
intro: Salarias fasciatus, commonly known as the jewelled blenny or lawnmower blenny is a benthic, neritic, marine fish species endemic to Australasia.

photo.author: Dirk Godlinski
photo.caption: Algae Blenny (Salarias fasciatus) in aquarium (Klimahaus Bremerhaven, Germany).

name: 睡衣天竺鲷
intro: The pajama cardinalfish, spotted cardinalfish, coral cardinalfish, or polkadot cardinalfish (Sphaeramia nematoptera) is a species of fish belonging to the family Apogonidae. It is a popular aquarium fish. 3 in) and features distinctive red eyes and a broad, dark, vertical 'waistband' with scattered red spots toward the tail.

photo.author: Brian Gratwicke
photo.caption: Pajama cardinal fish Sphaeramia nematoptera

name: 青蛙鱼
intro: Synchiropus splendidus, the mandarinfish or mandarin dragonet, is a small, brightly colored member of the dragonet family, which is popular in the saltwater aquarium trade. The mandarinfish is native to the Pacific, ranging approximately from the Ryukyu Islands south to Australia.

photo.author: Luc Viatour
photo.caption: Mandarinfish in aquarium-Muséum Liège (Belgium)

name: 白云金丝
intro: The White Cloud Mountain minnow (Tanichthys albonubes) is a hardy species of freshwater fish and coldwater fish often kept in an aquarium. The species was considered to be a member of the carp family (family Cyprinidae) of the order Cypriniformes, although now it is placed in the family Tanichthyidae.

photo.author: Nicklas Iversen (Corydoras-adolfoi); color adjustment: Togabi
photo.caption: White Cloud Mountain Minnow (Tanichthys albonubes), female

name: 蜜丽鱼
intro: The honey gourami (Trichogaster chuna) is a species of gourami native to India and Bangladesh.

photo.author: Antoondommerholt at Dutch Wikipedia
photo.caption: Honinggoerami (Trichogaster chuna, voorheen Colisa chuna)

name: 矮丽鱼
intro: The dwarf gourami (Trichogaster lalius) is a species of gourami native to South Asia.

photo.author: Felix Gertz
photo.caption: Picture of a male (left) and female (right) Dwarf gourami, Colisa lalia. The image depicts the natural colour variation.

name: 三点丝足鲈
intro: The three spot gourami (Trichopodus trichopterus), also known as the opaline gourami, blue gourami, and gold gourami, is a species of fish native to southeastern Asia, but also introduced elsewhere. This gourami gets its name from the two spots along each side of its body in line with the eye, considered the third spot.

photo.author: Gourami Watcher
photo.caption: A female three spot gourami (Trichogaster trichopterus)

name: 钻石虾虎
intro: Valenciennea puellaris, the Orange-spotted sleeper-goby, Orange-dashed goby, Maiden goby, or the Diamond Watchman goby, is a species of goby native to the Indian Ocean and the western Pacific Ocean.  It inhabits lagoons and outer reefs where it occurs over sandy substrates with larger pieces of rubble for it to burrow under.

photo.author: Rickard Zerpe
photo.caption: Maiden goby (Valenciennea puellaris)

name: 剑尾鱼
intro: The green swordtail (Xiphophorus hellerii) is a species of freshwater/brackish fish in family Poeciliidae of order Cyprinodontiformes. A live-bearer, it is closely related to the southern platyfish or 'platy' (X. maculatus) and can crossbreed with it.

photo.author: Corydoras-adolfoi
photo.caption: A male swordtail (Xiphophorus hellerii) fish.

name: 月光鱼
intro: The southern platyfish, common platy, or moonfish  (Xiphophorus maculatus) is a species of freshwater fish in family Poeciliidae of order Cyprinodontiformes.  A live-bearer, it is closely related to the green swordtail (X. hellerii) and can interbreed with it.

photo.author: Marrabbio2
photo.caption: Xiphophorus maculatus, female, rainbow wag variety

name: 花斑月光鱼
intro: The variable platyfish (Xiphophorus variatus), also known as variatus platy or variegated platy, is a species of freshwater fish in the family Poeciliidae of the order Cyprinodontiformes. A livebearer, it is native to southern Tamaulipas and northern Veracruz states in northeastern Mexico.

photo.author: Marrabbio2
photo.caption: Variatus platy (Xiphophorus variatus), male specimen.

name: 黄倒吊
intro: The yellow tang (Zebrasoma flavescens), also known as the lemon sailfin, yellow sailfin tang  or somber surgeonfish, is a species of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the family Acanthuridae which includes the surgeonfishes, unicornfishes and tangs.

photo.author: Luc Viatour
photo.caption: Yellow tang in aquarium-Muséum Liège (Belgium)

name: 紫倒吊
intro: Zebrasoma xanthurum, the purple tang or yellowtail tang, is a species of marine ray-finned fish belonging to the family Acanthuridae which includes the surgeonfishes, unicornfishes and tangs. This species is endemic to the north western Indian Ocean.

photo.author: Gdiggers
photo.caption: Purple Tang
